title: Circus bands, Steamer Capitol and cornet versus trumpet
summary: Father travelled with Barnum and Bailey 1907-1912, played the Steamer Capitol, funerals with Manuel Perez, blew a mouthpiece for $10 at Tom Anderson's; cornet until a trumpet at the end.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You mentioned a few minutes ago that he played in a lot of circus bands.

Oh, he traveled with Barnum and Bailey's circus for five years from 1907 until 1912. And he played on the Steamer Capitol. I have here the funeral parades with Manuel Perez. I remember him telling me an incident where when he was playing at Tom Anderson's, they paid him $10 to blow when day is done on his mouthpiece. Without the trumpet?
Do you remember, did he usually use a trumpet or a carnet that's a little bit shorter? A carnet. It was usually the carnet. In the beginning.
But when he died, he had a trumpet.
But years, all the years before that he had a carnet. He always called it a carnet.
